stem.en: Each sample below needs one of the two methods in this lesson. Sort each one into Spin it or Clump it.

text.en: Donated blood, to be separated into plasma and red cells
A large tank of cloudy pond water for a town to drink
A small tube of muddy water to be cleared in a few minutes
Tank water that stays cloudy after the heavier grains have settled
A thin tube of blood at a clinic with no electricity
Hot milk, with lemon juice added to make paneer

explanation.en: Spinning suits a small sample whose parts differ in density, such as blood or a tube of muddy water, and a paperfuge spins by hand. Clumping suits a large volume of cloudy water that will never fit in a machine: alum makes the fine grains stick and sink. Making paneer is clumping too, with lemon juice as the coagulant.

hints.en: Will the sample fit in a tube?
Is something being added to make particles stick together?
